title: Job Mindset Refresher (LT5) (course overview video)

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Conference room with a building floor plan, light meter and clipboard on the table; Matthew standing. Medium shot.
scenes.says: Welcome to LT5, Master Lighting Technician. At this level a lot of your work happens before the crew ever shows up: audits, light-level surveys, code checks, scopes, estimates and recommendations to customers. Your plan becomes everybody's plan. So we start this level the way we start every job, with the Job Mindset.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.on_screen:
1. Safety first  2. Plan the whole job  3. Think steps ahead
4. Keep every hand busy  5. Never be caught off guard
scenes.says: Five habits. Safety first, using the hierarchy of controls: remove the hazard before you reach for PPE. Plan the whole job before you leave the shop, worst cases included. Think several steps ahead. Keep every hand busy. And never be caught off guard. Here's how they apply to an audit.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Warehouse aisle with high bays; Matthew and a second tech with a lift parked and a clipboard.
scenes.on_screen: Scenario: audit a warehouse for an LED retrofit
scenes.says: Scenario: you're auditing a warehouse for a retrofit. Safety first: you'll be near high ceilings, forklifts and maybe energized measurements. Use the lift, not a tall ladder, coordinate with forklift traffic, and leave any energized readings to someone qualified and authorized, in the right PPE. Plan: floor plans, hours of operation, a meter, camera, and a checklist that includes ambient temperature.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Matthew photographing a fixture label from the lift basket while the second tech records data on a tablet.
scenes.says: Think ahead: the numbers you collect today become the crew's material list and labor plan. Wrong counts mean wrong parts on install day. Keep every hand busy: one person reads labels and counts, the other records, photographs and checks space types and controls. Nobody waits.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Matthew at the table, holding up a clipboard with a blank audit form.
scenes.on_screen: Common mistake: auditing only the easy areas
scenes.says: The most common mistake at this level is planning only the easy version of the audit. You count the main floor and skip the mezzanine, the freezer or the parking lot. Then the bid is short, the crew is short on parts, and the pressure to cut corners lands on install day. Plan the whole building.

scenes.speaker: Matthew Berrett
scenes.background: Matthew back in the conference room, facing camera.
scenes.on_screen: Never be caught off guard. Now begin the course.
scenes.says: Never be caught off guard: expect hidden fixture types, areas that run 24 hours, and a customer who asks for the payback on the spot. Plan for them, and your crew will never be surprised on install day. Use these five habits on every task in this level. Now work through the lessons and take the quizzes.
